_dayStop_comment: eval CHANGED 1500 -> 1000 on 2026-09-07. dayStop is documented in server.js (dayStopForContext) as 'the prop firm's max loss limit', and the firm changed: the new account is an APEX 50K EOD DRAWDOWN EVALUATION, which carries a FIXED $1,000 Daily Loss Limit (DLL). At $1,000 net intraday loss - realized AND unrealized - Apex auto-liquidates every position and pauses the account until the 6PM ET reset. 1500 was therefore a number the app could never actually reach: Apex would have flattened him 500 earlier. Hitting the DLL does NOT fail the account, it only ends the day. The number that FAILS the account is the EOD threshold below. Source: apextraderfunding.com help-center 'Daily Loss Limit Explained' (50K EOD eval row = $1,000; the DLL does not scale during an evaluation, only in a PA).

firmLimits._comment: DOCUMENTATION, not enforcement - nothing reads this block yet; it exists so the firm's real numbers live in the same file as the discipline rules instead of in someone's memory, and so a future drift check has something to compare against. Two DIFFERENT limits, routinely confused: (1) dailyLossLimit $1,000 is monitored intraday on total equity including open positions - hit it and Apex flattens you and pauses trading for the session, but the ACCOUNT SURVIVES and resumes at the next 6PM ET open. (2) eodThreshold is the one that KILLS the account: it is recalculated once per day at the close on the EOD balance, but is enforced intraday once set - touch $48,000 at any moment and it is immediate liquidation and evaluation failure. It stops trailing and freezes at $50,100 once it reaches the target-profit balance. There is no minimum number of trading days on the EOD eval. His own self-imposed stops (dailyLossTiers, perTradeMaxLoss 300) are far tighter than all of this and remain the operative numbers day to day - these are the outer walls, not the plan.

_sessionWindowsNote: Declared in each exchange's OWN timezone and converted to IST at load time by session-windows.js (see its header). Fixed IST minutes were wrong for half of every year: India has no DST, London and New York both do, and they shift on different dates. Durations are unchanged from the old fixed values (London 90min, NY 120min) — this moves WHEN a window opens, not how long it runs. Do not add startMin/endMin back here; loadRules() computes sessionWindowsIST from this block.

selectEval.label: Select Evaluation
selectEval._comment: 40% during the evaluation phase. The 3-day minimum is a consequence of the rule, not a separate gate: no single day may exceed 40% of total, so it cannot be passed in 1-2 days.

selectFunded.label: Select Funded
selectFunded._comment: Tradeify publishes NO consistency rule for Select once funded. null means 'no limit configured' — payout-eligibility.js treats that as not-computable rather than as automatically satisfied.

growthFunded.label: Growth Sim Funded

_lossRatchet_comment: ADDED 2026-08-12 (Anoop's own rule): tomorrow's maximum loss may never exceed what he made today. Targets his stated failure mode - 'after a couple of profit days, one day eats all my profits'. mode 'min' = cap is min(normal dayStop, yesterday's profit) - it can only ever TIGHTEN. This matters: the rule as first described ('max loss = yesterday's profit') would set an $800 cap after an $800 green day, i.e. 4x the $200 rule, loosening risk exactly after the good days that historically precede a blow-up. mode 'raw' would allow that; do not use it. floor = the cap never drops below this, so a tiny green day ($20) doesn't make tomorrow untradeable. A red or flat yesterday leaves the normal dayStop in force. warnAtPct = show a caution banner at this percentage of the cap.

_breakEven_comment: ADDED 2026-08-25, in Anoop's own words and his own numbers: "There are so many trades in a day that I take break even. Consider anything below 100$ and above -100$ as not a trade... After 5 break even trades, I want you to remind me." A trade landing inside +/-breakEvenBandUsd is flagged BREAK-EVEN and excluded from the real-trade count; at breakEvenReminderCount of them, mistake-patterns F4 fires. On 2026-08-25, 8 of his 11 trades landed inside the band - about $77.90 of commission paid for trades that returned nothing. DELIBERATELY ADVISORY: break-even trades STILL count toward tradesPerDay/contractsPerDay. Excluding them from a SAFETY cap would make churn - the exact thing F4 exists to flag - the loophole that bypasses the ceiling. It also does NOT enter the flags array: disc is computed as 4 minus the number of rule-break flags, so flagging BREAK-EVEN there would silently score a clean small trade as a rule break. WIDENED 2026-09-21: this band is now ALSO the definition of "a loss" used by the size-freeze guard (renderer/size-freeze-guard.js, called from grLog and grIngestLive) - a close inside the band is a scratch and cannot arm the size-up-after-a-loss stop. It was not, and on 2026-09-21 that fired the full-screen DAILY STOP HIT on a +$124.30 day over a 1-lot -$0.90 scratch followed by a 4-lot entry, with the trade count (4/10), the size (4/4) and the daily stop all intact. One number, one meaning: if -$0.90 is not a trade for the Journal and not a loss for the streak gate, it cannot be a loss for the freeze guard either. The guard FAILS SAFE on this key being absent or 0 - it then treats every negative close as a loss (the pre-2026-09-21 behaviour), unlike the renderer's display band which defaults to 100.

_playbooks_comment: ADDED 2026-08-26. The numbers playbook-spec.js needs to turn a detected setup into an actual entry/stop/target. They were previously nowhere: the live monitors fired a candle name and no trade plan at all, so no signal the app has ever recorded had an entry price, a stop, or a risk figure attached. stopBufferPoints and targetR come from the two Pine backtests already in Prop Trading/ (Playbook_A_C_Backtest_v2.pine and Playbook_B_JadeCap_SFP_FVG_Backtest_v1.pine both default to 3.0 pts and 2.0 R) so the JS harness starts from the same assumptions the Pine ones did, and any divergence in results is attributable to the logic rather than to the risk model. targetR is a PROXY for the rulebook's real exit ('exit at marker levels'), which is a hand-drawn zone no code can read - read backtest results as 'does the entry+stop edge exist', not 'does my exit process work'. fvgFillWindowBars is how long a Playbook B limit entry stays live waiting for the retrace before the setup is abandoned unfired; it is deliberately SHORTER than the SFP monitor's 8-candle patience window measured from the raid, because the clock here starts at the gap. outcomeHorizonBars mirrors SIGNAL_OUTCOME_HORIZON_BARS in server.js - change both together or the live ledger and the backtest stop being comparable, which defeats the point of sharing the detectors. minRiskPoints ADDED 2026-08-26 from the first real backtest run: 5 of 15 detected Playbook B setups came back with a stop exactly equal to stopBufferPoints, meaning entry==SFP wick, meaning the raid candle and the third candle of the displacement FVG were the SAME BAR - no displacement leg, so not the playbook. All 5 lost. 8 points is a judgement call, not a measured optimum: it is comfortably above the 1.0pt round-trip slippage assumption and above the 3pt buffer, and it is the number to revisit once there are more than 8.5 days of bars behind it. Setups under it are counted and reported, never silently dropped.
_contracts_comment: ADDED 2026-09-08 (G10). Per-symbol contract specs for risk pricing. pointValue must never be hardcoded in JS; resolve it from this block by the row's symbol and REFUSE on unknown symbols.
_flattenBy_comment: ADDED 2026-08-26 (Anoop, verbatim): "all the trades should end by 3 am indian stand time. the trades should not be carryied over night." 180 = 03:00 IST in minutes past midnight, the same units as sessionWindowsIST. This is a HARD FLATTEN, not a preference: any position still open at the cutoff is closed at the market, whatever it is showing. It also silently constrains every playbook - the backtest horizon of 12 bars on 30M is 6 hours, so a setup arming after 21:00 IST cannot be given its full horizon, and backtest.js now closes those trades at the cutoff rather than letting them run past it and reporting a result that could never have happened. Overnight gap risk on a prop account is uncapped by the intraday drawdown rules that otherwise protect him, which is why this is a rule and not a habit.
_playbookCAdx_comment: RENAMED 2026-09-01 from `dshV2` to `playbookCAdx` at Anoop's instruction ("name it playbook C (ADX)"). Config for the long-only ADX-gated breakout — see 'DSH backtesting/' and app/scripts/verify-dsh-strategy.js. The spec id is `C-ADX`, NOT `C`: `C` is the engulf validity gate and autonomy-modes.js aliases an incoming 'C' to 'LTF-ENGULF', so three things would answer to one key. See playbook-spec.js's header for the full reasoning. shadowOnly:true and liveSize:null remain the load-bearing values - this strategy has NEVER traded and nothing here may place an order. shadowSizes REMOVED: it was [4,6] and superseded on 2026-08-29 by autonomyModes.<mode>.sizes ([2]); leaving a dead sizing key in this file invites a future reader to change it and wonder why nothing happens. CHANGED 2026-09-04 (Anoop): 1H + lookback 5 — the dominant 2-contract cell. tfCode/tfLabel/lookback/adxMin all live in this block so he can change them without touching code. (Was kept as published lookback 10 / adxMin 35, even though a re-run at 2 contracts on 2026-09-01 shows they are the WORST of the consistency-safe cells: at 2c lookback10/ADX35 gives +$3,051, PF 1.95, consistency 40% - exactly ON the eval's 40% limit - while lookback5/ADX35 gives +$4,021, PF 2.17, consistency 30%, dominating it on all three axes at once. The dominated config is being forward-tested ANYWAY because re-tuning to the best cell of a grid before a single forward trade exists is precisely the curve-fit the research file warns against; the published claim gets tested as published, and lookback 5 is a candidate the forward data may promote, not a change to make on in-sample evidence. dailyCapPer2Contracts scales with size and enforces the 40% consistency rule.
_autonomyEnabled_comment: SET FALSE 2026-08-26 at Anoop's instruction ("disable shadow mode and control mode until i start working on them and have a proper plan... i want only you mode from now on"). RE-ENABLED 2026-09-01 at his instruction to forward-test Playbook C (ADX) - which is the proper plan that condition asked for, and it is the FIRST strategy here with out-of-sample evidence. _autonomyModes_comment: ADDED 2026-08-29 (AUTONOMY_MODES_SPEC.md). 2026-09-01: shadow.enabled flipped TRUE to forward-test Playbook C (ADX); assist and control stay false and therefore stay unrendered. Shadow is GLOBAL - it hooks armSetup, so A, B and LTF-ENGULF record alongside C-ADX. That is deliberate (Anoop, 2026-09-01: "i do not have issue if same live feed is fed to both the modes"): a record of the new rule with no record of the rules he already trades gives nothing to compare it against, and silent:true means the extra rows cost him no attention.  Per-mode flags UNDER the autonomyEnabled master switch, so the four modes can be finished and turned on one at a time. A mode with enabled:false is NOT RENDERED AT ALL - not a greyed-out button; a visible switch that does nothing invites a click that silently fails. sizes:[2] everywhere replaces the old dshV2.shadowSizes [4,6], which was the reason shadow had produced ZERO scored orders in its entire life: at $300 perTradeMaxLoss and $2/point, 4c allows only a 37.5-point stop and 6c only 25, while real Playbook B stops measure a 48.3-point median (range 38.8-72.8, see app/scripts/risk-dist.js), so EVERY setup was stamped blocked:risk-too-big and excluded from the resolver. 2 is Anoop's real sizeCap and sizeFloor, so the record needs no translation to be believed. shadow.silent was TRUE from 2026-08-29 and is now FALSE (2026-09-01, Anoop: "All the data when goes to shadow should be from live feed so that actions and signals are give to me immediately"). This REVERSES the August silence decision knowingly: silence was the fix for tickets confusing him mid-session on 2026-08-26, and un-silencing brings that risk back. What makes the trade acceptable is that he now has a live OFF switch he did not have then - OFF and SHADOW both render, so he drops to "you are trading" for his New York session and re-arms after, per-session, no restart. Silence hid the signals for ~8 weeks; a toggle he controls gets him the signals AND a way to stop them, which is what he actually asked for. If tickets start confusing live sessions again the fix is to use the toggle, or set this back to true - not to remove the feature. CONTROL's perTradeRiskCapUsd is 200, deliberately TIGHTER than the global perTradeMaxLoss of 300: its dailyLossCeilingUsd is also 200, and a daily limit is only a CEILING if per-trade risk divides into it - at the general $300 cap a single stop-out could lose $291 and overshoot the stated ceiling by 46% before anything could halt it. At $200/trade and $200/day CONTROL gets exactly ONE full loser per day and the ceiling is real (overshoot is slippage only). Cost: it skips the widest ~33% of Playbook B setups. autoResetDaily:false is Anoop's decision of 2026-08-29 - once tripped, CONTROL stays demoted to SHADOW until he personally re-arms it, because a breaker that resets on a timer lets a bad week run five unattended days. NOTE evidence read FOR CONTROL must filter shadow rows to riskUsd <= 200, since SHADOW records under the looser $300 cap. 2026-09-01: control.playbooks trimmed from [A,B,LTF-ENGULF] to [A,B]. Not a reduction in scope - every always-on engulf watcher (1H/30M/15M/5M) is now Playbook A, so LTF-ENGULF names nothing and listing a retired id in the allowlist of the one mode that can send real orders is exactly the kind of stale grant that gets overlooked. It also removes a real oddity: LTF-ENGULF was flagged unsanctioned in playbook-spec.js - present in no rulebook and no Pine script - while sitting on CONTROL's permitted list.
_eval_comment: CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 from Tradeify's own help centre (help.tradeify.co/en/articles/12853921-select-evaluation-accounts). Anoop trades 50K SELECT Evaluation only; his account TDFYSL…(account-id redacted) carries the SL/Select prefix, matching the selectEval payout tier already configured below. Every figure here is quoted, not inferred - the previous 150K numbers (9000/4500) had been in force on a 50K account, and my own earlier back-fit of start=50378.60 is REPLACED by the real 50000: back-fitting the start from the broker balance minus the ledger silently absorbs whatever the ledger is missing, and the ledger only begins 2026-08-17. A visible gap is better than a hidden one - the drift warning now surfaces it honestly. drawdownType: END OF DAY trailing, not intraday - 'intraday swings do not move the limit', but 'the limit is still enforced in real time - touching it fails the account immediately'. floorLocksAt 50100 = start+100, where the trailing floor stops rising. dailyLossLimit: null is REAL and is the dangerous part - SELECT Evaluation has NO broker-side daily loss limit, so nothing outside this app stops a bad day until the 2000 drawdown is gone. maxContractsBroker 40 is the BROKER's micro ceiling (4 mini / 40 micro); rules.json sizeCap of 2 is Anoop's own and is 20x tighter - the broker will never enforce it for him. minTradingDays 3 follows from the 40% consistency rule, not a separate gate.

oversizeGuard._comment: 2026-09-15 (Anoop: "i do not want any guard budget. it should be ON until i turn it off"): maxPerDay raised from 6 to 999999, i.e. effectively NO daily cap. He was mid-test when the guard had used 5 of 6 and he did not want a spent guard deciding he could not be protected again that day. What still bounds a runaway, unchanged and NOT to be weakened: confirmReads 2 (two consecutive polls must agree), cooldownMs per position, and the ONE-OUTSTANDING-REDUCTION rule - nothing further is sent until the position is SEEN to have shrunk, so time passing can never be read as evidence a fill happened. The daily counter was the outward bound; those three are the inward ones.

_oversizeGuard_comment: ADDED 2026-08-28 and ARMED LIVE at Anoop's explicit instruction after oversize cost him 72% of his 50K drawdown in a single session: day net -1436.20, of which -1147.70 came from the two trades over the 2-lot cap, and -1322.00 from one size-5 short. He chose REDUCE-TO-CAP over flatten (the thesis survives, only the excess risk goes: that short becomes about -529 instead of -1322, and the size-3 long that MADE +174.30 keeps 2 lots instead of being closed), TWO confirming reads before acting, and live arming rather than a shadow period. This is the only thing in the app besides handleTradeConfirm that can send an order, and the only one that does so unasked. It can ONLY reduce: the order is always strictly smaller than the position and always in the closing direction, so it is arithmetically incapable of opening or flipping one. It refuses to act on an unreadable size or an unreadable side - the fold logged size:0 four times on 2026-08-28 while real positions were open, and this repo's rows carry UNSIGNED sizes with the direction in a separate field, so inferring direction from the sign would have doubled a short instead of closing it. maxPerDay and cooldownMs bound a runaway: selling three lots every five seconds would be far worse than the problem it fixes. sizeCap is NOT duplicated here - it is read from the top-level sizeCap, so there is one size rule in this file, not two. Set enabled:false to disarm; every action is logged to DATA/protocols/oversize-guard.jsonl with the size observed, the order sent and whether the broker accepted it.

autoProtection._comment: ADDED 2026-09-15, EXTENDED 2026-09-21. App-side protection: the app watches the live position and flattens it at the per-trade stop and target (position-protection.js), because a broker-side bracket has no route on this build (order ticket not mounted). 2026-09-21 the band became PER-STAGE (eval vs funded) and gained a TRAILING STOP: once unrealised profit reaches breakEvenAtUsd, the protective stop rises to max(break-even, peak - trailDistanceUsd) and only ever rises, so a winner can no longer round-trip into a loss and a runner is banked automatically instead of being closed early by hand. trail runs only when BOTH trail numbers are positive; leave them blank/0 for the fixed -stop/+target behaviour. Dollars, not points (point value from the contracts block). The flat stopLossUsd/takeProfitUsd keys still work as a fallback for any caller that predates the split.
autoProtection._status: computation BUILT + tested (app/position-protection.js resolveAutoProtection + decide trail). APP-SIDE ONLY: protects while this app is awake and the broker feed is readable; a broker bracket would survive the app closing.

satisfaction._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (prop-firm doctrine). Deva's most repeated advice: pick a $ band that satisfies you, close at it, and physically leave the desk. This app has always been able to say he was DOWN too much — it had no way to say he was UP ENOUGH, which is the half that actually ends his days. $300 is HIS OWN documented number (Prop Trading/CLAUDE.md rule #4: 'Daily target: $150-$300 -> hit $300 -> strongly consider stopping') and sits inside Deva's stated $290-330 band, so nothing new is invented here: an existing number becomes machine-checkable for the first time. Read by app/day-plan.js, the guardrail HUD (state line + a once-per-day banner) and every agent's account context. ADVISORY ONLY — it never blocks a trade and never touches the day stop; it is the sentence he has never had from this app: today is already a good day, and the next trade can only take it away.

evalPlan._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19. Deva's eval method: break the profit target into daily chunks ($3,000 -> $750 x 4 days) and win on pace, not on hero days. 'days' is the ONLY number here — the chunk itself is computed live from the account's remaining distance to target (rules.json eval.profitTarget against the live balance), so it self-updates as the eval progresses and can never go stale the way a hardcoded '$750/day' would. 4 matches both Deva's stated 3-4 day plan and the arithmetic on this 50K Apex EOD eval ($3,000 / 4 = $750). Shown in the HUD and in every agent's context, eval stage only.

streakGate._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (Anoop's request: 'after 2 consecutive losses, show remaining-stops-until-DLL before the next entry'). afterLosses CHANGED 4 -> 2 the same day he asked for the surface: 4 was the placeholder, 2 is his number and matches F2's own 'two losses in a row = close the platform'. After N consecutive losses the HUD and every agent state the remaining room in STOPS rather than in dollars: how many full per-trade stops are left before the daily loss limit, and (when no DLL is configured) how many the whole drawdown is. 'You have $600 of room' is a number he has to translate under pressure; 'three full stops and the day is over' is the same fact already translated, at the moment it matters. A scratch (pnl === 0) ENDS a streak — it is not a loss (see day-plan.js's consecutiveLosses). Advisory only; F2's consecutive-loss detector still fires its own message, and no guard reads this value.

postPayoutRelapse._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19. Deva's warning, in his words: after his first payout he blew three accounts on 'it's easy, I did it before' — overtrading, stopped waiting, entering early. The app had no concept of a payout window at all. F5 (mistake-patterns.js) fires on the FIRST day inside this window that shows a known relapse signature: a size above the cap, a size-up while the day is red, or a trade count at the rulebook's own caution checkpoint. windowDays counts TRADING days with recorded activity after the most recent payout in account_fees.json (never calendar days — a payout followed by a two-week break is not a two-week window). overtradeAt 5 is not invented here: it is the checkpoint Prop Trading/CLAUDE.md's Session Warning Triggers table already names. Advisory only, once per signature per day, on the same channel as F1-F4.

escalateBands._comment: ADDED 2026-09-20 after the TypeSafe docs deep dive. The official confidence-routing pattern is explicit that a threshold belongs to the ACTION and not to the model — its own example checks a balance at 0.6 but demands 0.85+ to approve a transfer, because thresholds differ by what a wrong call costs. One global band was saying a routine Playbook A fire and a Playbook B confirm carry the same consequences. B is the highest-conviction event this app produces and the one that can surface a TRADE_TICKET, so its band is WIDER (0.45-0.95): more willing to pay for a second opinion, because missing a B verdict costs more. A is routine and gets a NARROWER band (0.6-0.9): fewer debates bought. escalateBand stays as the fallback for any playbook not listed, including one imported later. Read by typesafe-router.js escalation(); every decision reports bandFor so it always names which band judged it.

router._comment: PHASE 2, ADDED 2026-09-19. The shadow setup router (app/typesafe-router.js): on every ARMED setup it asks Jev ONE typed choice question — 'which ENABLED playbook does this state most resemble?' — with the enabled setups as the options, and writes the answer to DATA/signals/<day>.router.jsonl keyed by setupId next to the signal ledger. It ranks what Anoop READS FIRST and nothing else: it never vetoes a signal, never touches size, stop, or the confirm path, and no guard reads this block. It is a SEPARATE switch from typesafe.enabled so the journal classifier can run without paying for a call per setup — a router call is O(armed setups per day), which is the expensive shape, so it stays off until its measurement earns the spend. minConfidence is the floor below which a read is recorded but not shown as a ranking. escalateBand is the confidence WINDOW in which a second opinion (debate/judge) is worth firing: below it the read is too vague to be worth a slow answer, above it the mechanical gates already cover the case. Evaluate with evaluateRouter() — the ranking is only allowed to reorder the display when agree/disagree buckets have non-overlapping Wilson intervals, and if they never separate the correct action is to delete the router.

typesafe._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (Anoop: 'i want to use this inside the project'). TypeSafe's Jev is a hosted System One model that evaluates a STATE against TYPED QUESTIONS and returns typed answers with probabilities — it generates no prose, sees no images and calls no tools. So it is NOT an agent and NOT a provider for groq-agent.js: it is wired OUTSIDE provider-chain.js deliberately, so the one-provider rule (and the fallback alarm that goes with it) stays untouched and no agent can be silently answered by a third vendor. enabled:false until an API key exists in ~/.trading-copilot-config.json (typesafeApiKey) or TYPESAFE_API_KEY — and the client FAILS OPEN regardless, so every path is silent until then. maxCallsPerDay is a spend guard, not a technical limit. NOTHING consumes the answers yet: this is a shadow phase whose only job is to build a record that can be measured against his own outcomes before anything depends on it. Its 'confidence' is derived from how peaked the answer distribution is — it is NOT calibration, must never be quoted to him as a percentage chance, and must never reach a risk number.
typesafe._backend_comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 after Anoop hit the gate: TypeSafe's own console is INVITE-ONLY (console.typesafe.ai/login?error=ohnoes), so 'jev-latest' on api.typesafe.ai is unreachable for him in practice. The same model IS reachable on OpenRouter via POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with the OpenRouter key this machine already holds — verified with real calls on 2026-09-19, answering in the IDENTICAL typed shape (noul / choice+probabilities+confidence / score+legend) plus a per-call 'cost' field. A chat/completions call to these ids is refused by the vendor ('it is a decisions model'), which independently enforces the no-prose-agent rule. Two backends exist in app/typesafe-client.js (BACKENDS); this key selects one, and the client looks for the matching key field only — openRouterApiKey / OPENROUTER_API_KEY here, typesafeApiKey / TYPESAFE_API_KEY for the direct backend — so switching backends can never send one vendor's key to another vendor's host. Set 'backend':'typesafe' and 'model':'jev-latest' to go back if access is ever granted.
typesafe._status: Phase 1 (journal note classification, app/typesafe-journal.js, fired on note-save) and Phase 2 (the SHADOW setup router, app/typesafe-router.js, fired from armSetup) are both BUILT and both switched OFF. Notes land in accounts/<slot>/typesafe_notes.json, router reads in DATA/signals/<day>.router.jsonl, every call in DATA/typesafe/calls.jsonl. No guard reads any of it. The ONE remaining step is the key: add openRouterApiKey to ~/.trading-copilot-config.json (or set OPENROUTER_API_KEY), then set typesafe.enabled / typesafe.router.enabled to true.

mistakeTaxonomy._comment: The rubric Jev classifies a day against. DATA, like every other threshold in this file — changing what counts as a mistake is an edit here, not in code. The descriptions ARE the criteria the model reads, so each is written as an OBSERVABLE condition ('took another entry inside the cooldown after a loss') rather than a label ('revenge'), because a label the model has to interpret is a label it will interpret differently from Anoop. 'none' is deliberately treated as a first-class answer: a clean red day must be classifiable as clean, or the taxonomy teaches the model that every loss has a culprit — which is exactly the misreading this app exists to prevent. Consumed by app/typesafe-journal.js only.

options.revenge re-entry: Took another entry inside the cooldown after a loss, or re-entered the same level immediately after being stopped out.
options.sized up while losing: Increased the size of a later trade while the day's running P&L was already negative.
options.oversized: Traded more contracts than the per-entry size cap he was working to.
options.overtraded: Took more trades than the cap he had set for the session or the day.
options.chased entry or entered early: Entered before his setup completed — without the confirmation he requires, or several candles before the marked level.
options.held loser: Kept a losing position open past the point his thesis was invalidated or past his time stop.
options.cut winner early: Closed a winner before the level he had planned to exit at.
options.moved stop: Widened or removed a stop after the entry was taken.
options.traded both sides: Took longs and shorts in the same session, reversing with the market rather than with his bias.
options.traded outside the session window: Traded before the window opened or after it closed.
options.no pre-marked zone: Entered at a level that was not marked before the session started.
options.break-even churn: Took trades that closed inside plus or minus $100 — commission paid for trades that returned nothing.
options.none: His process held up: a setup he had written down, size and count inside his caps, and the market simply disagreed.

stateLevels: steady — describes the plan and the execution plainly, without urgency
pressured — describes wanting the money back, impatience, or frustration at the market
tilted — describes chasing, repeating an entry, or overriding a rule he had already set
mistakeTaxonomy.mistakeQuestion: Which single mistake best describes this losing day, judged from what he wrote and the trades listed? Choose 'none' when his process held up and the market simply disagreed — do not assign a culprit just because the day was red.
mistakeTaxonomy.stateQuestion: How far did his state move from his own baseline across this session, judged only from the words he wrote?
mistakeTaxonomy.planQuestion: Did he trade the plan he committed to before the session — the setups he wrote down and the trade cap he set — rather than what the market offered him in the moment?
mistakeTaxonomy.setupQuestion: Was the entry he describes an actual setup by his own written definition, rather than an early or chased entry he talked himself into?

voiceRouter._comment: ADDED 2026-09-21 (docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing + confidence-routing; see app/COMPOSITE_SCORING_PLAN.md and app/voice-intent.js). Voice used to send EVERY spoken word through the full Jessi agent turn -- persona, tools, whole account context -- when much of what he says into the mic is a command or a request for a number the app already holds. This classifies one utterance into one handler with a confidence, using the docs' own voice-banking shape: below the floor nothing is routed at all and the full agent answers (today's behaviour, unchanged); a read above the floor is safe to act on; an ACTION needs to clear its own higher threshold and is still spoken back before it is performed. mode: 'observe' records every decision and changes nothing; 'steer' (current) additionally hands the agent a one-line hint about what he is asking for, which shortens and focuses the spoken answer without this module ever inventing a number itself. Thresholds and descriptions are overridable under intents{}; an intent whose precondition is absent (an armed setup when nothing is armed) is not offered as an option at all, because the model cannot choose what it was never given. FAIL-OPEN at every step: disabled, no key, 503, malformed answer, unknown intent -- all of them resolve to 'the agent answers', so a router problem costs speed, never an answer.

weights._comment: ADDED 2026-09-21 (docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring, see app/COMPOSITE_SCORING_PLAN.md). The setup router used to ask ONE Choice question, which returns a rank and no breakdown -- when it ranked B above A there was no way to ask WHY, and no way to weight trend agreement more heavily without rewriting an instruction string. Now four atomic Scores are asked on the SAME request and combined here, in code. These weights are the only thing that decides the blend, so changing one is a data edit: no prompt rewrite, no redeploy. trend_alignment carries the most because the HTF gate already treats direction agreement as the veto, and level_quality next because 'no pre-marked zone' is a named mistake in his own doctrine. Fractions need not sum to 1 -- combine() renormalises over the dimensions that ANSWERED, so a state with no session read is judged on the three it has rather than dragged toward zero by the one it does not.

dimensions._comment: Level descriptions can be overridden here; the module's defaults are used for any dimension not listed. Level 0 is the low end and the order IS the numbering. Every level is judged against the state on its own, so each is written as a concrete situation rather than as a degree of a hidden scale. Max 10 levels (the API's ceiling).

levels: The higher-timeframe read is unclear, mixed or missing
With the recorded trend and the trend is itself strengthening
No identifiable level in the state
A level the detector inferred, not one he had marked
A level he had marked before the session
A major level he had marked before the session, at a prior swing
At the very edge of a session window, or in a thin period
Inside a session window, in its first hour
No trigger recorded, or the setup was invalid
A marginal trigger - the candle is present but does not fully qualify
A clean trigger that meets the written conditions
A textbook trigger: full qualification and clear displacement

playbookRegistry._comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (Anoop: 'i want to import many more playbooks in future which can be turned OFF or ON in the app'). THE ONE PLACE that answers 'is Playbook B on?' — before this, three files answered it and none agreed: playbook-spec.js said what they ARE, detectors.js said which ones fire, autonomyModes.control.playbooks said which ones a mode may trade. Two independent axes per playbook: 'enabled' = may it fire and be shown at all; 'shadowOnly' = may it ever place an order. They are separate because the only way to stop being nagged by a bad playbook must not also be the only way to stop MEASURING it — a playbook nobody measures can never be judged. Playbook C is a validity GATE (playbook-spec.js isGate), not a setup: it is locked ON in code and normaliseEntry() forces enabled:true, because switching it off would not disable a strategy, it would disable the FILTER on Playbook A and trade bare engulfs. A NEW playbook added here starts OFF and recording-only (NEW_PLAYBOOK_DEFAULT) and is labelled 'unknown' in the UI until a spec and a detector exist — so 'it is listed' is never mistaken for 'it is wired'. Sizing is clamped to sizeCap server-side on every write; nothing in the registry can widen the cap. The switch is HIS to flip; app/playbook-registry.js decideSwitch() only advises, and only from his own scored signals (n>=30 AND the Wilson LOWER bound above break-even AND positive expectancy per contract). Read by app/playbook-registry.js; consumed by the router's eligible list and by canExecute()/autonomy-modes.

C-ADX.note: Out-of-sample backtest evidence (DSH backtesting/), no live sample. Recording stays available from the C-ADX watcher; off because it has never been armed live.

_sizeCapBounds_comment: ADDED 2026-09-04 (Anoop: "make size changeable from 2 minimum to 6 as maximum size so that i always use it and not go beyond 6 size. i can handle 6 but yesterday i took 20 size which was unacceptable"). sizeCap is now HIS to move from the app, between these bounds; these bounds are not. stage-rules.js caps them again at a hard 2..6 in code, and getActiveRules() applies the ceiling AFTER the stage and scalper layers, so no overlay, hand-edit or rules-set message can produce an effective cap above 6. This LOOSENS the cap of 2 that his own data supports (see _sizeCap_comment and stageRules.funded._comment: every funded size except 2 loses money, -$1,717 over 31 trades) and that trade is made knowingly — on 2026-09-03 he traded 20 lots against a cap of 2, so the cap was not being enforced by agreement at all. A ceiling he trades inside beats a lower one he ignores. sizeCap itself is left at his current value on purpose: raising a risk limit is his decision to make, not a side effect of adding the control.
